title: Traces of powers of canonical ideals
summary: Let $(R,\m)$ be a one-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring with a canonical fractional ideal $R\subseteq K\subseteq\overline R$, and let $v$ denote its embedding dimension. Put $σ(R)=\sup\{j\ge0\mid\tr(K^j)\supseteq\m\}$. By definition, $R$ is nearly Gorenstein if and only if $σ(R)>0$. We prove that $R$ is almost Gorenstein if and only if $σ(R)\ge v$, equivalently, $σ(R)=\infty$. Thus every finite value of $σ(R)$ is at most $v-1$. We then determine the structure of rings for which $σ(R)$ attains its largest finite value $v-1$, just below the threshold for the almost Gorenstein property.…
